paragraphs: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda were so called, as in Taanit 23b; Rav Nachman, as in Megillah 28b; and Rabbi Zeira, as in Chullin 122a.[^1]

notes.text: The named Davidson Taanit 23b passage explicitly gives חסידי דבבל רב הונא ורב חסדא, supporting the contextual ר״ה expansion to Rav Huna. Full רב is also supplied for Chisda and Nachman. The separately read Davidson Chullin 122a episode has full רבי זירא followed by the pious-ones comparison, supporting Rabbi Zeira for this occurrence. Neither exact expansion comes from familiar identity alone. כ־ is represented by as in at each citation. כג:, כח: and קכב. give 23b/28b/122a by convention; Megillah 28b has not been freshly collated. Machine בן versus supplied כן and final comma versus period remain provenance differences, not source repairs. The heading is collective, not a single-person identity.
